analysis: Both changed files are documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/developer/test.md. No executable code, auth, attestation, encryption or billing paths changed. The edits describe how post-load KV headroom is measured: the check now reads one sample of the owner's GlobalKVCacheBudget (postLoadKVHeadroomBytes) in ensureModelLoaded, instead of KVHeadroomProbe.hasServeableKVHeadroom reading live machine memory. The invariant #5 cross-reference changed to KVHeadroomProbe.measuredLiveKVHeadroomBytes. The test doc says ScriptedProviderMemory scripts the sample for TinyModelCheckpoint tests. This touches only availability and memory admission (provider-side load gating); it has no direct link to T-041 or the TB-007 confidentiality items. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the doc text. Caveat: the source changes behind this wording (ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift, KVHeadroomProbe.swift, GlobalKVCacheBudget) are not in this batch. If a later pass sees them, check that the shared-sample change cannot let a post-load headroom check pass when real OS memory is short, and that the test-only scripted memory source cannot be reached in production builds. Nothing here rests on a visible code line; this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
